previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal injury, neurogenic bladder with urostomy, type II diabetes, peripheral neuropathy, and left transmetatarsal amputation was admitted for worsening left leg and foot pain, swelling, and a non-healing heel ulcer that began as a blister. Imaging showed no osteomyelitis. Her pain was managed with gabapentin, avoiding narcotics due to prior substance use concerns. She was treated with a short course of oral antibiotics for the ulcer after initial IV vancomycin, and wound care education was provided. A urine culture returned positive for Klebsiella after discharge, prompting a call-in prescription for nitrofurantoin. She also had transient chest pain likely from coughing and smoking, resolved without intervention, and symptoms of a viral upper respiratory infection treated supportively. Tobacco cessation support was offered. Due to housing instability, she was discharged to a medical respite shelter with follow-up arranged at Healthcare for the Homeless.
